import html from typing import List # Example template; in real code this would be defined elsewhere. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{headline}

Posted by: {poster_name}

{text}
{tags}
""" def compose_post_html( poster_name: str, headline: str, text: str, hashtags: List[str] ) -> str: """ Construct an XSS‑protected HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- poster_name : str Name of the author. headline : str Post title. text : str Main content of the post. hashtags : list[str] Tags associated with the post. Returns ------- str Safe HTML string ready to be rendered. """ # Escape all user supplied fields to avoid injection safe_poster = html.escape(poster_name, quote=True) safe_headline = html.escape(headline, quote=True) safe_text = html.escape(text, quote=False) # Preserve line breaks # Wrap each tag in a and escape the tag text safe_tags = [ f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in hashtags ] tags_html = ' '.join(safe_tags) # Format the final HTML using the template try: return USER_POST_FORMAT.format( poster_name=safe_poster, headline=safe_headline, text=safe_text, tags=tags_html ) except KeyError as exc: # Log or re‑raise with context if template is malformed raise ValueError(f"Missing placeholder in USER_POST_FORMAT: {exc}") from exc
